Q: EdgeBrowserControl firing events too often? A:

The control wraps WebView2 but exposes the old WebBrowser event names, which don't map cleanly. No navigation event can know when a 15-second server-side script finished. Only the page can tell you. Cleaner approach is to have the page signal it. End your PHP output with:

<script>window.__done = true;</script>

Then poll like below, as it doesn't depend on document.body timing:

If .RetrieveJavascriptValue("String(window.__done === true)") = "true" Then

Minor thing, use String(...) as it simpler to check with new Boolean(...).toString() workaround for the same result, as everything comes back as string.

Q: Best Way to Specify Linux Distribution Repo Version of Python Dependencies? A:

Have you perhaps explored using Red Hat Trusted Libaries? It's designed for the case where you need secure Python packages supported from Red Hat that aren't packaged via DNF. It seems like the best way to get to a broader set of packages while still getting Red Hat support. Last I looked, you get access if you have a Red Hat account, even with a no-cost RHEL for Business developers subscription.

https://developers.redhat.com/blog/2026/02/27/red-hat-trusted-libraries-trust-and-integrity-your-software-supply-chain

Q: Capacitor+Vite: when including Filesystem plugin, get warning “Unable to read file at path public/plugins”, then fails on import A:

This all came from my misunderstanding of Vite’s “project root” and its input and output directory settings, and the webDir setting in capacitor.config.json. After I fixed those two as described below, all the plugins are found correctly. The Capacitor warning about not finding public/plugins was a red herring.

Solution for my situation (but see “Better solution” below):

  1. In vite.config.js, include root: 'www/'– this needs to be the your source document root, not the top project root. When converting from a Cordova project, the document root is normally www/under the project root. The Vite documentation under Specifying Alternative Root was a bit unclear to me-- the vite.config.jsonly needs to live in the alternate root directory when that alternate root is given on the command line, e.g. npx vite build www, but better is to just put vite.config.js in the project root with root: 'www/'pointing to the document root, then run a plain npx vite build from the project root.

  2. In capacitor.config.json, set "webDir": "www/dist". It refers to the output directory of npx vite build, and is used as the input directory to npx cap sync. It’s set in vite.config.js as build.outdir, and it defaults to "dist"under what Vite calls the “project root” but which I’m calling the source “document root” here, to distinguish from the top project root. The npx cap init command suggests"www" for webDir, but you need to set it to the output directory of npx vite build, relative to where you run npx cap sync, thus the "www/dist"if you’re using Vite’s default build.outdir.

Better solution:

If you’d rather use a Vite output directory that’s not under the source document root (probably a good practice, but not the default), then make these two changes instead:

  1. In vite.config.js, include:
    root: 'www/',
    build: {
        outDir: '../dist/',
        emptyOutDir: true,
    },

This sets Vite’s build output directory to dist/ under your project root (outDir is relative to root), and emptyOutDir tells Vite to clear the output directory before the build. If you don’t do this, your build will contain output files left over from previous builds. (If your outDir is under the rootdirectory, emptyOutDir is set automatically, so we didn’t need it in the solution above.)

  1. In capacitor.config.json, set "webDir": "dist" to point to the new dist/as input to Capacitor commands.

Q: How to find d, given p, q, and e in RSA? A:

I think it's easier to visualize in a tabular format than over verbosity (both inputs are primes so an inverse definitely exists) :

r := remainder from truncated division

t := Bézout coefficients


        (old) t   (new) t   (new) r  (old) r    oT x nR      oR x nT  oTnR - oRnT

---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

1           1         -3    271412  [2490599]    271412     -7471797   [7743209]
2          -3         28     47891    271412    -143673      7599536   -7743209

3          28       -143     31957     47891     894796     -6848413    7743209
4        -143        171     15934     31957   -2278562      5464647   -7743209

5         171       -485        89     15934      15219     -7727990    7743209
6        -485      86986         3        89      -1455      7741754   -7743209

7       86986   -2523079         2         3     173972     -7569237    7743209
8    -2523079   [2610065]        1         2   -2523079      5220130   -7743209

                 2610065 := 2490599^-1 (mod 7743209)

First thing that jumps out as an invariant is the right most column of

old-bezout x new-remainder - old-remainder x new-bezout

Because its absolute value always matches original modulus, with alternating signs. In fact, every column other than the new and old remainders exhibit sign alternation. You can potentially even end the looping 1 cycle sooner :

old-bezout(row7) - new-bezout(row7)

 2610065 = (86986) - (-2523079)

ps : If you wanna see all the swapping action in-place, the expression looks like this

    _nt_ = _t_ - (_t_ = _nt_) * (_r_ \
 - (_nr_ = _r_ % (_r_ = _nr_))) /_r_

Since the remainder is always pre-subtracted out from the dividend / numerator, the division at the tail end of the expression is always integer exact.

caveat : This works in languages that use truncated division, such as awk or rust. Unsure whether pre-subtracting out a floor-div'ed modulo would wreak havoc with bezout's identity or not.

Q: Htaccess rewriting rule for localhost A: 
RewriteRule https://www.sanatariol.com(.+)\.html$ index.php?_htaccess_url=$1&%{QUERY_STRING} [L]

The RewriteRule directive matches against the URL-path only (not the absolute URL). So, the above rule will not match.

Try the following instead:

RewriteRule (.+)\.html$ index.php?_htaccess_url=$1 [QSA,L]

You also don't need to manually append the query string, use the QSA (Query String Append) flag instead.

Q: Author vs Contributor for R package - which role for small code contribution? A:

As pointed out in previous answers, the idea was to distinguish how substantial the different code contributions are. The manual page ?person explains:

The new scheme also adds the possibility of specifying roles based on a subset of the MARC Code List for Relators (URL: https://www.loc.gov/marc/relators/relaterm.html). When giving the roles of persons in the context of authoring R packages, the following usage is suggested.

  • "aut" (Author) Use for full authors who have made substantial contributions to the package and should show up in the package citation.
  • "cre" (Creator) Use for the package maintainer.
  • "ctb" (Contributor) Use for authors who have made smaller contributions (such as code patches etc.) but should not show up in the package citation.

Suggestions for the usage of further roles in the context of R packages are also provided there ("com", "cph", "ctr", "dtc", "fnd", "rev", "ths", "trl"). The citation mentioned above is the "default" or "auto" citation that you get from citation("foo") if package "foo" has no dedicated CITATION file. If it has you can still get the default by citation("foo", auto = TRUE). See ?citation for more details.

Coming back to the question of "author" vs. "contributor": When we wrote the documentation above (and the accompanying paper by Hornik et al. in The R Journal) we deliberately just gave rough guidelines because the ultimate decision what is "substantial enough" needs to be made by the package authors themselves. This is not unsimilar to the decision who to include in the author list of a scientific paper vs. mentioning in the acknowledgments - for which the practices also vary a lot across disciplines/communities.

A strategy that is not uncommon is to distinguish three levels of contribution:

  • Those who made very small contributions (like small fixes or improvements) are not listed in the DESCRIPTION but acknowledged in the NEWS or Changelog. This applies to many small contributions made through bug/issue trackers or small pull requests on GitHub or similar platforms.
  • Those who provided larger patches, small helper functions, additions for specific cases, etc. who should be listed in the DESCRIPTION as "contributors" (ctb). This also applies to the case where code parts are copied from other packages or other sources.
  • Those who made larger and/or continuing contributions that are substantial enough to be listed as "authors" (aut) in the DESCRIPTION and the package's default/auto citation.

Reference: Hornik K, Murdoch D, Zeileis A (2012). "Who Did What? The Roles of R Package Authors and How to Refer to Them." The R Journal, 4(1), 64-69. doi:10.32614/RJ-2012-009
